subject: Provisional uptime adjustment & SLA mitigation plan for Arbortech pilot
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <marta@arbortech.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@arbortech.com
Date: 2027-06-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot request: temporary uptime tolerance & credit structure

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is keen to move forward with a 3-month pilot starting July 1. Before we finalize the Statement of Work, Procurement has a hard constraint: our integration window and expected traffic pattern for the pilot will likely push peak infra into a lower-availability SLA class.

Can Redwood consider a temporary uptime tolerance of 99.0% for the pilot period (vs your standard 99.95%) and swap the standard one-size service credit for a graduated remedial credit schedule + a short-term committed-capacity discount?

We attached an estimated usage workbook so you can see expected request patterns (prod-usage-estimate.xlsx). We appreciate that this is non-standard — happy to discuss conditions that would make this acceptable on your side (monitoring, quarterly rollback, credit caps, etc.).

Appreciate a quick read — we need commercial terms to present to our CFO by next Wednesday.

Best,
Marta
Marta Ruiz
Head of Vendor Ops, Arbortech

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta@arbortech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-05T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot request: temporary uptime tolerance & credit structure

Hi Marta — thanks for the details and the workbook. I reviewed the numbers briefly and I think we can put together a limited pilot proposal, but it will require a Deal Desk / Exec exception.

High level I propose we consider:
- A provisional uptime target of 99.0% for the 90-day pilot only
- Graduated service credit schedule that scales by severity and is capped at X% of monthly fees (we'll define cap with Deal Desk)
- A short-term committed capacity discount for the first month of the pilot to offset integration risk
- Mandatory telemetry/heartbeat monitoring and weekly review calls during the pilot window

I'll loop in Marissa from Deal Desk to scope the commercial trade-offs. Can you confirm the CFO deadline (time zone) and whether Arbortech can accept a rollback to standard SLA if production exceeds the risk threshold? Also please confirm that the attachment in the workbook is correct.

Regards,
Sofia Ivanova
Account Lead, Strategic Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-06T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: FW: Pilot request: temporary uptime tolerance & credit structure

Team — FYI and ask. Arbortech (potentially strategic, regional presence in EU + US) is requesting a 90-day pilot with a provisional uptime target of 99.0% (standard is 99.95%). They want the usual service credit swapped for a graduated remedial schedule and are asking for a short-term committed-capacity discount for month one.

Attachments they provided: prod-usage-estimate.xlsx. I also drafted a short pilot SOW and proposed remedy outline (pilot-sow.pdf, proposed-remedy-terms.docx).

What I need from Deal Desk + Finance + Legal:
- Marissa: proposed commercial compromise (discount band, credit cap).
- Ben: suggested credit cap (%) and exposure modeling for 99.0% for 90 days — operational risk and expected max credit liability.
- Jonas / Lauren: Exec approval path — this is a non-standard SLA tweak; we should keep the exception limited to pilot and include firm telemetry + weekly reviews.

Constraints we should bake in:
- Remedy cap no greater than 25% of monthly spend for the pilot period (subject to finance),
- Automatic reversion to standard SLA + pricing if pilot metrics exceed thresholds or at 90 day end,
- Clear monitoring instrumentation and access for Arbortech to confirm incident counts.

I recommend we keep legal language tight and require sign-off before July 1 if we're to meet their timeline. Marissa — do you have capacity to pull a draft term sheet by EOD tomorrow?

Thanks,
Sofia

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-07T14:37:00-07:00
Subject: RE: FW: Pilot request: temporary uptime tolerance & credit structure

Sofia — thanks for the heads up. I reviewed the numbers in prod-usage-estimate.xlsx and ran a quick exposure calc. High level thoughts:

1) Commercial compromise: we can offer up to a 20% committed-capacity credit for month 1 (applied as a one-time invoice credit), in exchange for the provisional 99.0% pilot SLA.
2) Remedy schedule: propose a graduated credit: 5% credit for severity-2 incidents, 12% for multiple day outages, capped at 20% of monthly invoice for the pilot window.
3) Financial cap: Ben please validate — I expect exposure under reasonable assumptions to be below 18% of projected pilot spend, so the 20% cap feels safe.
4) Legal: redline required to restrict this exception to a single pilot and to include explicit telemetry & audit access for Arbortech.

If Execs sign off on the 20% cap + pilot-limited clause, I can finalize a term sheet and push to Legal/Finance. We should also attach a clause for weekly operations review and a rollback clause after 30 days if incidence exceeds threshold.

Marissa
Director, Deal Desk
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-09T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Approval: provisional SLA exception for Arbortech pilot (conditions)

All — after reviewing the ask and the proposed guardrails, I approve a provisional exception on the following conditions only: 

1) Exception is timeboxed: 90 days only, starting on the pilot start date specified in the SOW. No roll-forward without a fresh exec review.
2) Credit cap is set at 20% of monthly fees for the pilot period. No uncapped credits.
3) Mandatory telemetry: Arbortech must enable the agreed monitoring endpoints and grant Redwood read access to support incident validation.
4) Weekly ops sync for the pilot and a 30-day automatic rollback trigger if incident rate exceeds the threshold defined in the term sheet.
5) Legal to insert explicit language limiting this to this pilot and specifying remedies; Finance to confirm the 20% cap modeling.

Marissa — please finalize the term sheet with these conditions and loop Legal and Finance. Once Legal signs off on the wording we can route a one-off amendment to the MSA.

Jonas Weber
VP, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
